comment_box:
I comment on the following excerpt:
'For the avoidance of doubt, the proposed rule would make clear that the exclusion for abortion does not apply “when a physician certifies that the life of the mother would be endangered if the fetus were carried to term.” This is also consistent with the pre-2022 regulations for the CHAMPVA program.
No State law prohibits treatment for ectopic pregnancies or miscarriages to save the life of a mother.'

Carrying a non-viable pregnancy to term can pose serious physical and emotional risks to mothers. The lives of pregnant mothers are endangered to some degree by every pregnancy, viable or not. If this rule wants to consider the safety of mothers, then the rule should be clarified to add that the exclusion for abortion does not apply when a physician certifies that a fetus is non-viable. It is in the interest of the safety of mothers that non-viable pregnancies be terminated either medically or surgically (e.g., induced miscarriage), should the mother choose to do so in consultation with her physician. It is better to allow this option as a choice prior to the mother's potential appearance in the emergency room with sepsis, and the VA should provide this medical benefit as part of its benefits package.
